chunks.arabic_text: وَ رُوِيَ عَنِ الْعَلَاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ :

translations.en: And it is narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي الرَّجُلِ يُعْتِقُ غُلَامَهُ أَوْ جَارِيَتَهُ عَنْ دُبُرٍ مِنْهُ ثُمَّ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى ثَمَنِهِ أَ يَبِيعُهُ

translations.en: Regarding a man who emancipates his male slave or his female slave as a mudabbar after his death, then comes to need his price—may he sell him?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ لَا إِلَّا أَنْ يَشْتَرِطَ عَلَى الَّذِي يَبِيعُهُ إِيَّاهُ أَنْ يُعْتِقَهُ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "No, unless he stipulates to the one to whom he sells him that he emancipate him at the time of his death."

en.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on the sale of a slave who has been declared mudabbar, meaning designated for emancipation upon the owner's death. The Imam عليه السلام forbids selling such a slave unless the seller makes a condition upon the buyer that the emancipation be carried out at the buyer's death.
en.seo_question: Can a mudabbar slave be sold if the owner later needs the money?

key_terms.يُعْتِقُ: to emancipate or free from bondage
key_terms.عَنْ دُبُرٍ: as a posthumous emancipation arrangement, effective after death
